I'm attempting to munge some summary statistics.  I have no trouble when using the Hapmap 3 reference panel. However, using Hapmap results in the loss of about 17% of the SNPs (don't know if that's typical or not--this is an ancestrally diverse sample). munge(files=files, hm3=snplist, trait.names=trait_names, N=n_eff)
.

Katherine

messages.subject_clean: userGWAS error: unequal length of vector
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

While running userGWAS function for a factor in the hierarchical model, I have encountered the error below. Would there be a solution to this error?

Loading required package: GenomicSEM
There were 24 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
[1] "Please note that an update was made to userGWAS on 11/21/19 so that it combines addSNPs and userGWAS."
[1] "Starting GWAS Estimation"
Error in .userGWAS_main(i, int, n_phenotypes, n, I_LD, V_LD, S_LD, std.lv <http://std.lv>,  :
  task 1 failed - "'names' attribute [23] must be the same length as the vector [21]"
Calls: userGWAS -> %dopar% -> <Anonymous>
Execution halted

Below is the code that I ran and I have attached ldsc output and sumstat output RData to reproduce the error. Sumstat output contains only the first 1,000 SNPs.

require(GenomicSEM)

ldsc.out <- "M_ldscout.RData"
sumstat.out <- "M_sumstat_subset.RData"

load(ldsc.out)
load(sumstat.out)

model <- "F1 =~ NA*V8 + V7 + V6 + V3
        F2 =~ NA*V1 + V2 + V6 + V5 + V3
        F3 =~ NA*V4 + V5 + V6
        M =~ NA*F1 + F2 + F3
        M ~~ 1*M
        V5 ~~ a*V5
        a > 0.001
        M ~ SNP
        "

MetS.GWAS <- userGWAS(covstruc=M_ldscout,
                          SNPs=M_sumstat.subset,
                          estimation="DWLS",
                          model=model,
                          cores=20,
                          toler=1e-50,
                          SNPSE=FALSE,
                          sub=c('M ~ SNP'),
                          parallel=TRUE,
                          GC="standard",
                          MPI=FALSE,
                          smooth_check=TRUE,
                          printwarn=FALSE)

Best,

Austin

Hi,

Thank you for the remark!
By using unit loading identification, the userGWAS seems to work!

But I have another question regarding unit variance and unit loading identification for the model without SNPs. Shouldn't the model fit generated have identical values whether I use unit variance or unit loading identification? But I'm getting slightly different results.

This is how I specified the hierarchical model for unit variance identification.
model <- "F1 =~ NA*V7 + V8 + V6 + V3
F2 =~ NA*V2 + V1 + V6 + V5 + V3
F3 =~ NA*V5 + V4 + V6

F1 ~~ 1*F1
F2 ~~ 1*F2
F3 ~~ 1*F3

V5 ~~ a*V5
a > 0.001
"

model <- "F1 =~ 1*V7 + V8 + V6 + V3
F2 =~ 1*V2 + V1 + V6 + V5 + V3
F3 =~ 1*V5 + V4 + V6
M =~ 1*F1 + F2 + F3

V5 ~~ a*V5
a > 0.001
"

Austin

Hi Austin,

The independent pathways model can be specified to operate on the first order factors (rather than the higher order factors) or on the individual traits. You should interpret accord to which specification you use. I can imagine wanting to specify on the first order factors (so it's still a common pathways model through those factors but not through the higher order factor), and then from there specifying yet another independent pathways model to operate on the individual traits (or perhaps several, where you free up independent pathways for one first order factor at a time). That way you can get at heterogeneity at each level.

You can read through the 11 disorder paper by Grotzinger et al. in Nature Genetics to see the approach that we specifically took for the hierarchical p factor model.

I can't recall off hand what the defaults are for allowing independent variables to correlate with factors. When you run the model in some tests SNPs with your code you should make sure that the SNP doest covary with the factor(s) by default (you can always fix those covariances to 0 to be sure) in your independent pathways model.

Elliot

S is the genetic covariance matrix. You can use cov2cor in R to produce the genetic correlation matrix. However, you can request that the genetic correlation matrix and its associated sampling covariance matrix be outputted in the ldsc option by inputting stand = TRUE into ldsc().

Note that due to sampling variability you can sometimes get estimates that are out of bounds or a matrix that is nonpositive definite. If you are using corrplot you'll need to set is.corr to FALSE, or you'll need to smooth the matrix first using nearPD.
